answer: Steady Pace Gate requires each new identity to keep request gaps inside a strict timing shape for its first hundred actions before gaining full access. Bursts or gaps outside that shape are throttled at a bridge queue, so every extra identity costs an attacker real waiting time plus a distinct traffic pattern to maintain. Cheap parallel identities collapse because sustaining that rhythm across a saffron-marked lagoon of concurrent workers imposes per-identity delay and coordination cost.
